coverage: Named roster FETCHED: the Guardian/Alison Flood interview at the primary (the Tolkien Society page proved a relay of it); Pembroke College's report of the 2021 Tolkien Lecture; Katherine Olley's two Oxford talks, both read as their linked .srt transcripts rather than as page blurbs; the Locus "Margins of History" interview carrying Kay's Dunnett attribution; Dorothy Dunnett Society material (the centenary "Writers' Writer" collection, the Society biography, the Whispering Gallery contents) via Wayback raw captures after 403s; and Kay's own Locus "In Memoriam - Dorothy Dunnett", which turned out to join angles 1 and 3 - he met Dunnett in spring 1975 through a letter found inside the Tolkien correspondence he was editing. NOT FOUND: no published text or transcript of "Just Enough Light" that I could locate; no review of Beyond This Dark House in a national outlet surviving online beyond Rettino's. BLOCKED: the lecture's own YouTube caption track (HTTP 429 on every timedtext fetch, tried twice and spaced apart), Tor.com's write-up (403), and the academia.edu Whispering Gallery paper (403 login wall); the session's WebSearch budget was exhausted mid-sweep and DuckDuckGo served a CAPTCHA, so the last third of discovery ran on bibliography chasing alone. Substantive sources per route: 12 by the named roster, 11 by bibliography chasing (Sacnoth's Scriptorium, then Noad from Rateliff; the brightweavings essay index paged to depth 6, which yielded the Dunnett memorial and the Fionavar afterword; tolkienlecture.org's write-up list; Olley's .srt files from her pages), 5 by Wayback recovery, 3 by lateral search. 31 sources read, 25 substantive, 113 claims, every quotation checked verbatim against the fetched text by script. Angle 1's third limb is the thinnest: no source I found argues explicitly that the Quenta and the Annals are the ancestor of Kay's historian-narrator; the nearest real connectors are Charles Noad's claim that Kay's contribution was the making of a finished narrative out of annalistic materials, and Rettino's independent finding that Kay's narrator speaks as a chronicler. I have not bridged them myself.
